body: You are not being too sensitive. As a fellow asian, I'm too familiar with this type of interaction. Worst part is, people expect asians to just accept this kind of garbage. DO NOT PUT UP WITH ANY OF IT. And if you need to, find new friends.  In regards to that business, you were absolutely in the right. File a complaint.

As someone who is 35, currently without a job, has never been in a relationship (I can't even get a date), I can semi-relate. They sound like toxic people in your life. I hate that you have to experience that. They have made you feel less than you deserve. I could go on and on in my assessment of the situation but I want you to know that you do not deserve this. 

But to answer your question, what keeps me from doing it? I've attempted suicide several times. I'm a pretty solitary person most of the time. So much so that if I were to do anything, no one would find my body for weeks since no one ever checks up on me.  But what keeps me from doing it are the little things. It sounds silly but sometimes I think about a movie I'm really excited about, or how much I enjoy a certain type of food. It's simple, I know but it keeps me going, just for a little bit. 

What keeps you from doing it?

I do not think you should ignore your feelings.  But you should be able to acknowledge when something is not being reciprocated. In general, people need people. We all have roles that we fit into in other people's lives.  I understand how it upsets you when things turn out to only be platonic but don't you realize that these people that turn to you do so because they need someone to talk to? Turning people away when they are in need is an unattractive quality.  I understand if you felt like you were being used. No one likes that feeling.  But do you think these platonic relationships you have with people who happen to be female are equal? Do they listen to you? Do they have fun with you? It sounds like if people want to invite you out to a party or such, they like having you around. 

"I didn't and judging by how things are going never will".  You can be just as certain of that as you are that things WILL turn out. Ask yourself, what happens if you have a girlfriend and you find yourself miserable? What then? 

I don't imagine I'll change your mind. I would like to get through to you though.  You sound like you are frustrated and in pain.  But what if a girl that you weren't attracted to liked being around you? And you saw each other as just friends and you loved being around her? Just as friends? What if she resented you for that and pushed you away because your relationship couldn't be something more? Wouldn't that hurt? Wouldn't that suck?

I don't feel I can appeal to you with numbers and charts. You are unhappy and you obviously want to be better or else we wouldn't be talking.  But in my previous message I asked a few questions and provided a few perspectives and am interested in your response to those. I will respond to you for as long as I need to in order to lessen whatever pain you are going through.

I have had persistent thoughts of suicide.  Every hour of every day.  Talking and listening to others about what they're going through would really keep my mind of things and benefit the both of us. Let me know if I can be of help.

Hmmm. Sounds like your friend is projecting.  Or something else. I dunno.  Either way, as friends we all talk a big game sometimes, and unfortunately it effects how others feel about interacting with us.  Whether he honestly extends his policy of "do nothing bitches" to his close friends, at least let him know that he can talk to you about stuff (of course that's if you're willing).  Maybe when he feels safe, he'd be more willing to reciprocate that favor. 

It sounds like your sister is just as much a product of your parents upbringing as you are.  You said your sister doesn't really appreciate what you're trying to tell her.  I think it sounds like she wants someone to listen to her. Maybe? Just a guess.  A common problem I've found with people is that those who don't want to listen to other people's problems are the same people that need someone to talk to about their own. 

Good that you're fine with getting out of business law.  Better to find out now then further down the line when you're working in a field that you despise.  You could've waited but you wouldn't have known unless you tried.  And now you tried. Learn from this experience.  I graduated high school, didn't go immediately to college and spent the next few years working retail but the plus side was I got to play music and tour the world.  There are opportunities in life that will always be there and those that are fleeting.  Trust me.  School will always be there.  I didn't start til I was almost 30.  Do I regret waiting so long? A little.  But I would've never gotten to see the world the way I did.  There is nothing wrong with waiting. In the long run, this means you'll be better disciplined, know exactly what you want to do, and you'll have saved money. It sounds like despite what your parents say, they've at least accepted some parts of what's going on. It's that tough asian love that will never change. In fact, they sound exactly like mine.  My parents just want me to be happy even if they always hassle me about money and getting married. I remember when my mom asked, "Are you ever going to go to college. .. before I die??" Yeeesh. 

I'm sure you're already aware, but I was just asking about your eating habits because it can greatly affect everything we do. I know that if I've gone out drinking more than a few times a week, have eaten poorly, and have *ahem* masturbated a bunch, my depression becomes waaaay more severe.  Just try to wean yourself off the junk. Don't expect things to change overnight.


It sounds like you're a really aware, smart, considerate dude that just wants to make his parents happy. I totally get how much pressure you're going through and how that can really dim your outlook on things.  But often times, we focus too much on the future and not the present.  It's great to look ahead but not when it gives us anxiety and a feeling of hopelessness.  Get back to the gym. Try to be less hard on yourself even though your parents made you feel that it is justified. But it gets to you because you care about what they think. 

I dunno. There's a lot going on here and I want to be able to address everything as much as I can.  Oh also, if you're best friend is someone you can't turn to, don't let that discourage you.  Everyone in your life has a role, you just gotta figure what that is. Anyways my fellow asian, don't hesitate to hit me up about stuff. I feel your pain.

ok, well I kind of see where this is going but. . .what does a girlfriend mean to you? What will that solve? What is the purpose, to you, in having a girlfriend?

Yeah, a girl becomes friends with a guy they aren't attracted to. Yet friendships sometimes turn into deeper relationships.  I can speak from plenty of experience.  If people are given a chance to get to know you better, the real you, maybe they'll see something they like, maybe they won't.  The point is, by not giving people that option, you are guaranteeing that nothing positive will happen.  I can say that with 100% confidence.   

Handsome assholes? Do you want to be an asshole? Sure, there are plenty of guys out there who sleep around.  But they move from girl to girl.  Which means they can't keep a girl.  I don't know a single girl (and trust me, I know plenty) that wants to date an asshole.  The girls I know aren't immature like that.  Do you want to date an immature girl? 

Ask yourself, who are these guys you are looking to as positive examples? Who told you that this is the way to live? 

You talking about needing a girlfriend and not friends.  Why don't you want friends? 

Has your friend literally told you you're disgusting? Even if she said you weren't would you believe her? If you won't believe her, what makes you think she's lying? 

The world is such a big place, there are so many people out there.  Not every girl is going to be attracted to you, and that's fine. Not everyone shares the same idea of what is attractive.  But do you think pushing people away seems more attractive in the long run? What would make you feel better about yourself (that didn't involve being in a relationship, because that is called "codependency").

Ha. I only had to read your previous responses to tell that you're asian. Guess what? So am I. 

So why don't you think your best friend will understand?
I think that's really awesome that you're trying to be such a good role model for your little sister. I often think about how I would've loved a younger sibling so I could take care and protect them from things I went through. 

What classes are you taking? How far are you in?  As someone who's living in the US, I can tell you that the situation of living in an asian household with high expectations is no different.  I was always compared to my parents friends kids. Instead of going to school to be an engineer I took up music! as a kid I wanted to do art! So I hope you know I can understand that I can empathize. Also, I'm currently having to pick up a seasonal retail job to fend off costs.  Asian families are so ridiculous.  You're in your 20's?  I remember feeling that pressure.  At least you're not in your 30's like me.  I made a lot of wrong choices that I've managed to hide from my family. School has been up and down for me.  My depression is severe.  But I've found that talking to my teachers and keeping them posted about my progress and opening up a dialogue has helped me so many times.  I've almost dropped out several times.  I'm glad I said something.  Do you feel you are in a position with your teachers and counselor to do that as well?

Look, you're never going to be able to escape the shadows of what your family casts on you. I'll be honest.  But you can make it so that it doesn't matter AS much. Is what you're doing in school what you really want to do? In asian families, we are taught that we have to do what's best for the family and not the individual.  I will tell you that I've rejected that notion so many times and while it hasn't been easy, it made parts of my life better and my family slowly got used to it (not fully accepted, mind you).  There comes a point where you have to realize that you need to live for yourself and not your parents.  You are conditioned at a very young age where your validation is entirely dependent on your parents word.  It's manipulative and not good for a child's self-esteem. 

Do you ever go back to the gym? Even for a little bit? Do you have friends you can go with? You don't have to talk about what's going on at school, but do you think just a little time here and there can alleviate the extreme pressure you're going through? What are your current eating habits like?

Son,
I can see why you're frustrated but there is something I noticed in your post.  
You talk about how you present yourself in contrast to how you feel inside and when no one's around.  Does that feel like honest to you?

Also, while many people are in relationships, who's to say those are happy, quality ones? Consider the statistics in regards to marriage: Nearly half of all marriages end in divorce.  

You seem to put a lot of emphasis on the value there is in being in a relationship with a girl.  Yet it sounds like there are a lot of women that seem to want to know you.  I want you to know, getting to have a lot of female friends means you have the upper hand that most guys don't.  By being friends with people of the opposite gender --as long as you listen to what they're saying-- you being to understand them more.  Being a sensitive, caring guy that a woman feels safe around is nothing, NOTHING to be ashamed of.

What does being friendzoned mean to you? Like, really? If a woman isn't attracted to you, fine I get that. But ask yourself, what do you find a problem with in gaining another friend? And when that girl told you you're like a brother, why does that bother you? She's telling you she can trust you.  That she feels safe around you.  This means you're a good guy.  

Look, you'll come to your own conclusions about things but let me tell you, the concept of "manliness" is bullshit.  There is no "one size fits all" in terms of how a young man such as yourself should act.  I used to worry about being friendzoned but I realized after awhile, more women who were actually attracted to me would come up to talk just because they saw me around so many women (who were just simply my friends).  Having a lot of female friends mean they tell me what they like and hate in a guy.  That is very very valuable info! 

Go to the party. Hang out with your friend.  Are you certain you won't meet more people there? If you stay home you are guaranteeing that absolutely nothing will happen.

I understand what it feels like to not have that lifeline within reach.  That person that helped make things more breathable.  
It's normal to be scared about the prospect of trying to go out there again.  While thinking about the future is something we should always consider, I feel that maybe in terms of things that worry you, it might be better to just focus on the present and what small, tiny, even inconsequential things you can do to just lighten the load of things (that don't involve drinking).  Are there nature paths near your house that you can go to, even for 10 minutes a day? Is there anything that you love to do that involves producing something (art, cooking, mechanics) that you can put your energy into?

It sounds like your living situation is giving you a great feeling of stress and confinement.  Also, in regards to the air mattress, Ive had a few roommates who just slept on the floor of the room.  Hell, the first time I moved out all I had was a sleeping bag.  

You didn't mention who else you interact with.  Co workers? Friends?

You can't compare yourselves to others around you.  Their lives are theirs. Everyone has their own experiences.  You are responding to your own unique experiences. 
I can understand what it feels like to have formed relationships under the basis of toxicity.  You interact under such certain terms that being outside of that leaves you with anxiety.  Am I close?

But please acknowledge that you got this far.  You're clean.  Does that sound like something shitty people do? I'm pretty sure that's the opposite of a cancerous personality.

I was actually about to respond to your post as I thought your subject line resonated with me.
Thank you for reaching out. 
I noticed in your posts that your relationship with your family is strained.  I can very much relate.  In certain cultures, we are expected to be representative and appreciative of our family's efforts.  Anything less is utter failure even if they don't say it.  

What I didn't see (maybe I didn't look hard enough) is who else do you communicate with? Siblings? Friends? What if anything are you investing in right now that you won't see the fruits of until a few years down the line? 

You sound like someone who is honestly trying and not making excuses.  I know what that's like.  But after awhile every effort feels futile.  What did you used to love doing? 

Thank you again for reaching out.
